title: Introduce granular warmup allocator and quant-compat fallback layer
author: Priya Mehta
description:
Motivation: Cold-starts and tenant-tail workloads are a dominant contributor to per-token cost and latency variance in production. Existing warmup logic is coarse-grained (global prefill budgets per GPU pool) and interacts poorly with mixed quantization lanes (8/4-bit variants), leading to either wasted cold-prefill or unexpected quality regressions when aggressive quant profiles are selected. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) a Granular Warmup Allocator that assigns probabilistic warmup budgets per-tenant and per-shape window based on recent traffic and signalized unit-econ thresholds; (2) a Quant-Compatibility Fallback Layer (quant-compat) that detects when a chosen quant profile may produce outlier loss on sampled eval prompts and routes the request to a compatible fallback model/quant lane automatically.
Summary of changes:
- allocator: new service and runtime hook (warmup-allocator) that maintains lightweight sliding-window counters, probabilistic budget tokens, and an admission policy that prefers small, high-value prefill allocations; supports tenant overrides and a dry-run telemetry mode
- quant-compat: compatibility matrix + lightweight evaluator that runs a fast-loss heuristic on a small prompt set and consults policy rules to choose fallback variants; integrates with serving router to enforce graceful fallback and emits structured telemetry when fallbacks occur
- telemetry: new econ-prefill and quant-compat events, dashboards, and alerts (updated docs link below)
- config: new tenant-level fields for warmup_budget_mode, sample_rate, and quant_compat_policy
- CLI: warmup-sim tool to simulate budgets and visualize unit-econ impact
Motivation continued: the goal is to reduce wasted GPU tokens spent on prefill while bounding tail latency and preventing silent quality regressions from aggressive quantization.
Design notes:
- Probabilistic token issuance uses a reservoir with deterministic seeding per-tenant to enable reproducible sampling in A/B tests
- Shape windows are keyed by (model_family, sequence_bucket) to keep state small
- Quant-compat uses a two-stage check: quick divergence heuristic (latency < 2ms) + optional micro-eval (bounded to 5ms) before deciding fallback
- All decisions are logged and can be toggled to dry-run to collect telemetry before enforcement
Checklist:
- [x] Implementation of warmup allocator server and runtime hook
- [x] Quant-compat compatibility matrix and decision flow
- [x] Integration tests for allocator admission across tenant cohorts
- [x] Unit tests for quant-compat heuristics and fallback routing
- [x] Telemetry events and Grafana dashboard templates
- [x] Backwards-compatible config parsing and tenant override validation
- [x] Upgrade plan for existing clusters (migration steps in upgrade_notes.md)
Testing and results: In staging with three representative tenants (chatbot, search, assistant) we ran a 48h dry-run. Results vs baseline:
- Prefill token spend: -22% on average (peak -35% for search tenant)
- Tail 99.9 latency: improved 8-12ms for mixed-quant lanes
- Observed quality regressions from quant fallbacks: 0 (when fallback policy enabled)
- CI: all unit/integration tests green. See simulation artifacts in s3://redwood-econ/sim/582431/
Deployment and rollout:
- Start in dry-run on dedicated pools for 1 week to validate telemetry
- Enable enforced mode with conservative budgets and quant_compat_policy: "safe" rollout for next 2 weeks
- Expose tenant-level opt-outs for customers with strict prefill SLAs

release_notes: Introduce Granular Warmup Allocator (tenant/shape probabilistic prefill budgets) and Quant-Compatibility Fallback Layer. Reduces prefill token waste and provides safe fallbacks for aggressive quant profiles. Configurable tenant-level controls and telemetry. Rollout is gated behind feature flags.
upgrade_instructions: See docs/upgrade_notes.md. Short summary: enable dry-run feature flag in staging, monitor econ-prefill events for 48h, then enable enforced mode with conservative budgets. For Dedicated customers, run scripts/migrate-warmup-legacy.sh to backfill reservoir seeds.
notes_for_prod: Start in dry-run mode on 1-2 pools; watch prefills per-tenant and spike-throttle events. Default quant_compat_policy is 'safe' which prefers 8-bit fallback when divergence heuristics trigger. Use warmup-sim to validate tenant budgets before enabling enforcement.
